NHM / FEDERATION / PRIVACY
The implemented privacy boundary
ENGINEERING FEDERATION DEMO
RESEARCH PROTOTYPE
SIMULATED CLIENTS
NOT CLINICAL
NOT DEPLOYED
A narrow engineering claim about what the aggregation interface receives. It is not a general privacy or security guarantee.
01 / LOGICAL CLIENT
What stays local
Local synthetic training examples stay inside each logical client buffer. All eight logical clients execute on one demonstration machine, not separate hospitals or institutions.
02 / COORDINATOR
What the coordinator receives
Model updates and metadata — not the clients' local synthetic training examples. This is an application-level data-flow boundary, not host or network isolation.
03 / SHADOW
What SecAgg+ demonstrates
ROUND 1 ONLY
ROUND-1 PROTECTED-AGGREGATION SHADOW: a Flower SecAgg+ shadow is executed for round 1 only and compared with the plain aggregate under the frozen tolerance. Authoritative aggregation remains PLAIN in every product run.
TECHNICAL CLAIM BOUNDARY
What is not claimed
No differential privacy.
No anonymity guarantee.
No hospital deployment.
No network or host isolation claim.
No production security certification.

report.text:
NHM / ABOUT
About this prototype
A research monitoring prototype and a separate federated-development demonstration. These are engineering and scientific evidence boundaries, not medical claims.
01 / SCOPE
What NHM is
NHM is a research prototype for physiological monitoring and federated model development. It is not diagnostic and not a medical device.
Monitoring states are research outputs, not health assessments.
02 / MONITORING
What runs today
For model inference, the wearable source is SIMULATED ONLY (WEARABLE_SIM_V1). No physical wearable is connected to the inference path. A separate, optional MongoDB source displays ESP32 telemetry; the released model can be applied to it only as an experimental, resampled and not-valid analysis (Monitor, Observatory replay and trace, and optional federated fine-tuning of the pretrained V2 on your recorded windows with synthetic labels). The physical device path still requires a live hardware demonstration.
Inference is server-side: MODEL_V2_FINAL in SOFTWARE_SYSTEM_V2. Nothing runs on a sensor.
The virtual Monitor plots simulated source ECG. A PPG waveform is unavailable in the current simulator. The hardware view plots stored ECG ADC values against server ingestion time; its device-reported SpO₂ is unverified.
03 / DEVELOPMENT
Federated development
The engineering federation runtime is enabled. It runs eight logical, synthetic research clients (not hospitals or institutions) on one demonstration machine; each performs genuine local optimization and the coordinator receives model updates rather than local examples.
In a connected (Clerk) live run only, one existing synthetic client, SIM_FL_SITE_00, is shown as MY EDGE CLIENT - a presentation binding to the signed-in owner. Its training data is still synthetic engineering data: your physiology does not train any model, no personal or personalized model exists, and monitoring sessions are never federation data.
04 / BOUNDARY
What NHM does not claim
A federation run produces an engineering candidate that stays in a sandbox. It is never automatically deployed and does not replace the released MODEL_V2_FINAL.
No physical wearable validation, personalized model, or hospital deployment is established. NHM is not diagnostic.

The frozen models scored on 12-lead clinical ECG from PTB-XL (lead II, one 10-second window per record). NHM / ABOUT
About this prototype
A research monitoring prototype and a separate federated-development demonstration. These are engineering and scientific evidence boundaries, not medical claims.
01 / SCOPE
What NHM is
NHM is a research prototype for physiological monitoring and federated model development. It is not diagnostic and not a medical device.
Monitoring states are research outputs, not health assessments.
02 / MONITORING
What runs today
For model inference, the wearable source is SIMULATED ONLY (WEARABLE_SIM_V1). No physical wearable is connected to the inference path. A separate, optional MongoDB source displays ESP32 telemetry; the released model can be applied to it only as an experimental, resampled and not-valid analysis (Monitor, Observatory replay and trace, and optional federated fine-tuning of the pretrained V2 on your recorded windows with synthetic labels). The physical device path still requires a live hardware demonstration.
Inference is server-side: MODEL_V2_FINAL in SOFTWARE_SYSTEM_V2. Nothing runs on a sensor.
The virtual Monitor plots simulated source ECG. A PPG waveform is unavailable in the current simulator. The hardware view plots stored ECG ADC values against server ingestion time; its device-reported SpO₂ is unverified.
03 / DEVELOPMENT
Federated development
The engineering federation runtime is enabled. It runs eight logical, synthetic research clients (not hospitals or institutions) on one demonstration machine; each performs genuine local optimization and the coordinator receives model updates rather than local examples.
In a connected (Clerk) live run only, one existing synthetic client, SIM_FL_SITE_00, is shown as MY EDGE CLIENT - a presentation binding to the signed-in owner. Its training data is still synthetic engineering data: your physiology does not train any model, no personal or personalized model exists, and monitoring sessions are never federation data.
04 / BOUNDARY
What NHM does not claim
A federation run produces an engineering candidate that stays in a sandbox. It is never automatically deployed and does not replace the released MODEL_V2_FINAL.
No physical wearable validation, personalized model, or hospital deployment is established. NHM is not diagnostic.

Comparability audit (read-only)
Same model family — SAME: Both are the V2 TCN-mean architecture (MODEL_V2_FINAL vs FL V2 models).
Same evaluation windows / labels — SAME: Population report records identical ordered example ids across all 20 FL models; V2-010 prediction tables for the centralized V2 model hold 2157 (INTERNAL_TEST) and 26864 (INCART) rows, equal to these populations.
Same evaluation pass — DIFFERENT: Centralized values are historical frozen references; they were NOT re-run in the one-shot FL evaluation.
Threshold-free metrics only — SAME: AUPRC and AUROC do not depend on the decision threshold or calibration; F1/precision/recall were evaluated under different thresholds/calibration and are not compared.
Training procedure — DIFFERENT: Centralized: pooled training. Federated: 8 clients, 50 rounds, FedAvg; optimisation budget and selection path differ.
Paired uncertainty — NOT_AVAILABLE: No paired patient-cluster bootstrap exists between a centralized and a federated model; differences below are point differences with no interval.
Dataset exposure — LIMITED: INTERNAL_TEST is federated-lineage held-out but not project-globally unseen (6 clusters); INCART is a post-freeze second look on a project-exposed dataset.

Near parity on INTERNAL_TEST. Both AUPRC values exceed 0.998 (ceiling region); the point difference is in the fourth decimal. Limit: 6 clusters; ceiling effects make small differences uninformative; no paired interval.

NHM / RESEARCH OBSERVATORY / EXTERNAL CHECK
External check on real ECG no model had seen
The frozen models scored on 12-lead clinical ECG from PTB-XL (lead II, one 10-second window per record). PTB-XL was removed from the project's execution scope, so no model was ever trained, selected, calibrated or evaluated on it. This is an extension outside the locked scope: it has no beat annotations, so the target is record-level, and it is not a clinical or diagnostic result.
FROZEN EXTENSION EVIDENCE · REAL UNSEEN ECG · RECORD-LEVEL TARGET · NOT AAMI-SVF · NOT CLINICAL
Extension outside the locked AAMI_SVF_WINDOW_V1 scope: the dataset has no beat annotations, so the target is record-level (a cardiologist statement or an extra-beat field says the record contains premature beats). No model was trained, selected, calibrated or evaluated on this dataset before; fixed 0.5 rule, no calibration; no clinical, diagnostic or device claim.
21,535 records scored (paced records excluded: 302; no record lost to a missing lead, wrong length or flat signal: 0 excluded). Target PTBXL_PREMATURE_BEAT_RECORD_V1 · fixed 0.5 rule · calibration NONE.
Evaluation set
primary (folds 9-10)
replication (folds 1-8)
Models on primary (folds 9-10)
4,336 records, 476 with premature beats (prevalence 0.110), 3,809 patients; 95 % patient-cluster bootstrap intervals from 2,000 resamples. Label rule A (either label source). AUPRC depends on prevalence, so lift (AUPRC ÷ prevalence; 1 = chance) is shown beside it.

What this shows
The pretrained V2 ranks premature-beat records well above chance on data it never saw (AUROC 0.911, lift 6.4), and clearly better than V1 (V1's paired AUROC change against it is −0.210, interval [-0.237, -0.184], which excludes zero).
Adapting a model to a synthetic cohort lowers its performance on this unseen real ECG: original cohort AUROC −0.036, AUPRC −0.169 against the central V2; realistic cohort AUROC −0.046, AUPRC −0.229 against the central V2. A synthetic-cohort candidate is not a better ECG model than the released one.
Federated training on real patients matches centralized training in AUROC; see the paired change of the 50-round federated rows.
Label rules (primary set)
The two label sources agree on only part of the premature-beat records (1,052 both, 472 cardiologist statement only, 902 extra-beat field only, over all records), so the same models are scored under three predeclared rules. Point estimates.

Scope and boundary
STATEMENT
0.5 min

Three things are kept apart everywhere: frozen scientific evidence, a monitoring product, and an engineering demonstration.

This is not clinical or diagnostic. Synthetic and assigned labels are never expert ground truth.

LIVE · COMPUTED NOW
2 min

Choose the realistic cohort and 3 rounds from the pretrained start, then start. Narrate the eight logical clients, local training, aggregation and the per-round evaluation. Start it, continue to the next step, and return.

Local optimisation and aggregation are really executed on one machine, and each committed state is scored afterwards by a separate observer.
Say
Eight logical clients on one laptop with synthetic data: it demonstrates the mechanism, not a deployment.

Open the prepared completed run from "Your federation runs" and use its replay.
Open Federation Studio →

Independent evaluation of every round
PREPARED RUN · RECORDED

Understand
The evaluation cohort is disjoint from training, no round or threshold is selected from it, and a score on a synthetic cohort is a pipeline check, not a performance claim.
Say
These scores come from one synthetic cohort family. Over five repeated training runs round 10 beats the pretrained start there, but adapting to the synthetic cohort lowers performance on real MIT-BIH ECG, so a candidate is not a better ECG model than the released one.

Use any completed run; the layout is identical.

report.text:
NHM / ABOUT
About this prototype
A research monitoring prototype and a separate federated-development demonstration. These are engineering and scientific evidence boundaries, not medical claims.
01 / SCOPE
What NHM is
NHM is a research prototype for physiological monitoring and federated model development. It is not diagnostic and not a medical device.
Monitoring states are research outputs, not health assessments.
02 / MONITORING
What runs today
For model inference, the wearable source is SIMULATED ONLY (WEARABLE_SIM_V1). No physical wearable is connected to the inference path. A separate, optional MongoDB source displays ESP32 telemetry; the released model can be applied to it only as an experimental, resampled and not-valid analysis (Monitor, Observatory replay and trace, and optional federated fine-tuning of the pretrained V2 on your recorded windows with synthetic labels). The physical device path still requires a live hardware demonstration.
Inference is server-side: MODEL_V2_FINAL in SOFTWARE_SYSTEM_V2. Nothing runs on a sensor.
The virtual Monitor plots simulated source ECG. A PPG waveform is unavailable in the current simulator. The hardware view plots stored ECG ADC values against server ingestion time; its device-reported SpO₂ is unverified.
03 / DEVELOPMENT
Federated development
The engineering federation runtime is enabled. It runs eight logical, synthetic research clients (not hospitals or institutions) on one demonstration machine; each performs genuine local optimization and the coordinator receives model updates rather than local examples.
In a connected (Clerk) live run only, one existing synthetic client, SIM_FL_SITE_00, is shown as MY EDGE CLIENT - a presentation binding to the signed-in owner. Its training data is still synthetic engineering data: your physiology does not train any model, no personal or personalized model exists, and monitoring sessions are never federation data.
04 / BOUNDARY
What NHM does not claim
A federation run produces an engineering candidate that stays in a sandbox. It is never automatically deployed and does not replace the released MODEL_V2_FINAL.
No physical wearable validation, personalized model, or hospital deployment is established. NHM is not diagnostic.

report.text:
NHM / ABOUT
About this prototype
A research monitoring prototype and a separate federated-development demonstration. These are engineering and scientific evidence boundaries, not medical claims.
01 / SCOPE
What NHM is
NHM is a research prototype for physiological monitoring and federated model development. It is not diagnostic and not a medical device.
Monitoring states are research outputs, not health assessments.
02 / MONITORING
What runs today
For model inference, the wearable source is SIMULATED ONLY (WEARABLE_SIM_V1). No physical wearable is connected to the inference path. A separate, optional MongoDB source displays ESP32 telemetry; the released model can be applied to it only as an experimental, resampled and not-valid analysis (Monitor, Observatory replay and trace, and optional federated fine-tuning of the pretrained V2 on your recorded windows with synthetic labels). The physical device path still requires a live hardware demonstration.
Inference is server-side: MODEL_V2_FINAL in SOFTWARE_SYSTEM_V2. Nothing runs on a sensor.
The virtual Monitor plots simulated source ECG. A PPG waveform is unavailable in the current simulator. The hardware view plots stored ECG ADC values against server ingestion time; its device-reported SpO₂ is unverified.
03 / DEVELOPMENT
Federated development
The engineering federation runtime is enabled. It runs eight logical, synthetic research clients (not hospitals or institutions) on one demonstration machine; each performs genuine local optimization and the coordinator receives model updates rather than local examples.
In a connected (Clerk) live run only, one existing synthetic client, SIM_FL_SITE_00, is shown as MY EDGE CLIENT - a presentation binding to the signed-in owner. Its training data is still synthetic engineering data: your physiology does not train any model, no personal or personalized model exists, and monitoring sessions are never federation data.
04 / BOUNDARY
What NHM does not claim
A federation run produces an engineering candidate that stays in a sandbox. It is never automatically deployed and does not replace the released MODEL_V2_FINAL.
No physical wearable validation, personalized model, or hospital deployment is established. NHM is not diagnostic.

NHM / RESEARCH OBSERVATORY / EXTERNAL CHECK
External check on real ECG no model had seen
The frozen models scored on 12-lead clinical ECG from PTB-XL (lead II, one 10-second window per record). PTB-XL was removed from the project's execution scope, so no model was ever trained, selected, calibrated or evaluated on it. This is an extension outside the locked scope: it has no beat annotations, so the target is record-level, and it is not a clinical or diagnostic result.
FROZEN EXTENSION EVIDENCE · REAL UNSEEN ECG · RECORD-LEVEL TARGET · NOT AAMI-SVF · NOT CLINICAL
Extension outside the locked AAMI_SVF_WINDOW_V1 scope: the dataset has no beat annotations, so the target is record-level (a cardiologist statement or an extra-beat field says the record contains premature beats). No model was trained, selected, calibrated or evaluated on this dataset before; fixed 0.5 rule, no calibration; no clinical, diagnostic or device claim.
21,535 records scored (paced records excluded: 302; no record lost to a missing lead, wrong length or flat signal: 0 excluded). Target PTBXL_PREMATURE_BEAT_RECORD_V1 · fixed 0.5 rule · calibration NONE.
Evaluation set
primary (folds 9-10)
replication (folds 1-8)
Models on primary (folds 9-10)
4,336 records, 476 with premature beats (prevalence 0.110), 3,809 patients; 95 % patient-cluster bootstrap intervals from 2,000 resamples. Label rule A (either label source). AUPRC depends on prevalence, so lift (AUPRC ÷ prevalence; 1 = chance) is shown beside it.

What this shows
The pretrained V2 ranks premature-beat records well above chance on data it never saw (AUROC 0.911, lift 6.4), and clearly better than V1 (V1's paired AUROC change against it is −0.210, interval [-0.237, -0.184], which excludes zero).
Adapting a model to a synthetic cohort lowers its performance on this unseen real ECG: original cohort AUROC −0.036, AUPRC −0.169 against the central V2; realistic cohort AUROC −0.046, AUPRC −0.229 against the central V2. A synthetic-cohort candidate is not a better ECG model than the released one.
Federated training on real patients matches centralized training in AUROC; see the paired change of the 50-round federated rows.
Label rules (primary set)
The two label sources agree on only part of the premature-beat records (1,052 both, 472 cardiologist statement only, 902 extra-beat field only, over all records), so the same models are scored under three predeclared rules. Point estimates.

NHM / GUIDED DEMONSTRATION
One story, about 9 minutes
From a signal entering the monitor to measured, bounded evidence. Each step says what to open, what the audience should take away, how its evidence is produced, and what to do if it fails. A research prototype, not clinical or diagnostic.
LIVE · COMPUTED NOW
Computed on this machine while you watch (a simulated source or a real local training run).
PREPARED RUN · RECORDED
A run completed earlier in this workspace; opened, not recomputed. It carries its own RECORDED / replay labels.
FROZEN EVIDENCE · HASH-CHECKED
A committed report read after a SHA-256 check. Nothing is trained or re-evaluated.
RECORDED SESSION · STORED
Stored telemetry or a stored monitoring session; its labels and quality grades are shown as recorded.
STORED · DURABLE LIBRARY
Engineering candidates kept across restarts, verified against their digest before use.
STATEMENT
Scope and limits, said aloud.
1
Scope and boundary
STATEMENT
0.5 min
Do
State what NHM is: a research prototype with a released centrally trained model, a monitoring product, and a separate federated engineering lane.
Understand
Three things are kept apart everywhere: frozen scientific evidence, a monitoring product, and an engineering demonstration.
Say
This is not clinical or diagnostic. Synthetic and assigned labels are never expert ground truth.
If it fails
Nothing to fail; this is a statement.
Open About →
2
A signal enters the monitor
LIVE · COMPUTED NOW
1.25 min
Do
Attach the simulated wearable, start a session, and point at the quality state before any model result. Mention that a MongoDB hardware source exists and is shown only as a labelled, recorded session.
Understand
Windows are built causally, quality is graded before inference, and the released model answers per window.
Say
The wearable here is simulated. The hardware path is an experimental, resampled analysis that is explicitly marked not valid.
If it fails
Open the latest completed session from History; it is stored evidence.
Open Monitor →
3
Federated training, live
LIVE · COMPUTED NOW
2 min
Do
Choose the realistic cohort and 3 rounds from the pretrained start, then start. Narrate the eight logical clients, local training, aggregation and the per-round evaluation. Start it, continue to the next step, and return.
Understand
Local optimisation and aggregation are really executed on one machine, and each committed state is scored afterwards by a separate observer.
Say
Eight logical clients on one laptop with synthetic data: it demonstrates the mechanism, not a deployment.
If it fails
Open the prepared completed run from "Your federation runs" and use its replay.
Open Federation Studio →
4
Independent evaluation of every round
PREPARED RUN · RECORDED
1 min
Do
Show the evaluated rounds, the evaluation cohort label, the fixed 0.5 rule and the generalisation tab against the frozen V2 baseline.
Understand
The evaluation cohort is disjoint from training, no round or threshold is selected from it, and a score on a synthetic cohort is a pipeline check, not a performance claim.
Say
These scores come from one synthetic cohort family. Over five repeated training runs round 10 beats the pretrained start there, but adapting to the synthetic cohort lowers performance on real MIT-BIH ECG, so a candidate is not a better ECG model than the released one.
If it fails
Use any completed run; the layout is identical.
